dialect.detail: Likely GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) based on LINE SEQUENTIAL organization, GOBACK, SORT on table array, and no vendor-specific extensions. Could also be Micro Focus, but GnuCOBOL is most consistent with the feature set and file naming conventions.

purpose.domain_detail: Product transaction reporting — reads product catalog and transaction CSV files, matches transactions to products, and generates a formatted sales report
purpose.summary: GENREP reads a product CSV file and a transaction CSV file into in-memory arrays, sorts transactions by product ID, then generates a formatted report (report.rpt) showing per-product transaction details including quantity and line totals, with subtotals per product. It is a batch report generation program.

notable_features: OCCURS table with INDEXED BY and SEARCH (linear search)
SORT on in-memory table array (SORT WS-ARRAY-TRN)
LINE SEQUENTIAL file organization for CSV input
PERFORM VARYING with multiple UNTIL conditions
Formatted report output with $-sign edited PIC clauses
verdict.notes: The program has a fixed maximum of 5 products and 50 transactions hardcoded, debug paragraphs commented out, and an AUTHOR field of WORAMET — all consistent with a student exercise or coursework assignment. No COMP-3, no SQL, no CICS. The dialect cannot be pinpointed precisely without compiler directives, but GnuCOBOL is the most likely target given the feature set.
